operativeSourceText:
Section 1.01 of the Credit Agreement is
hereby amended by adding the following definitions in the appropriate alphabetical order:
“Invoice
Restrictions” has the meaning set forth in the Monthly Factoring Report.
“Maintenance Liquidity”
means, as of any date of determination, (a) the sum as of such date of (x) the aggregate amount of the commitments under the Super-Priority Revolving Credit Facility (including the aggregate revolving commitments with respect to any
Permitted Euro Revolving Indebtedness) (or any Refinancing Indebtedness in respect thereof) minus (y) the aggregate principal amount of the outstanding revolving loans under the Super-Priority Revolving Credit Facility and any
outstanding revolving loans in respect of any Permitted Euro Revolving Indebtedness (or any Refinancing Indebtedness in respect thereof) and, in each case, the face amount of any letters of credit issued thereunder (less any reimbursed amounts)
plus (b) the “Adjustment to Liquidity” as set forth in the most recently delivered Monthly Factoring Report plus (c) unrestricted cash and Cash Equivalents of the Borrower and its Subsidiaries.

“Monthly Factoring Report” means a report substantially in
the form of Exhibit E or any other form approved by the Administrative Agent.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: ADD[ DEFINED_TERM_REFERENCE "Super-Priority Revolving Credit Facility", METRIC_REFERENCE "Aggregate revolving commitments with respect to Permitted Euro Revolving Indebtedness (or Refinancing Indebtedness in respect thereof)" ] (exprId ir-expr:1db2d51e4ff33be672ba1c3e)
findings.verifierReasoning: The source text uses the word "including" to introduce the Permitted Euro Revolving Indebtedness commitments inside the parenthetical modifying "the aggregate amount of the commitments under the Super-Priority Revolving Credit Facility." "Including" language ordinarily signals that the item named is already a component/subset of the preceding aggregate figure, not a separate quantity to be added on top of it. The proposed IR instead models clause (x) as an ADD of two distinct operands - the Super-Priority Revolving Credit Facility commitments (as a standalone defined-term value) plus a separate Euro revolving commitments metric - which risks double-counting the Euro commitments (once inside the base facility figure, once again as a separate addend), thereby overstating (x) and consequently overstating Maintenance Liquidity. A hypothetical: if the SP facility's aggregate commitments figure already embeds $20mm of Euro-tranche commitments and the IR also adds a separate $20mm Euro-commitments metric, Maintenance Liquidity would be overstated by $20mm relative to the source's likely intended reading. I flag this UNCERTAIN rather than definitively MATERIAL because clause (y), by contrast, uses "and" (not "including") to join the SP and Euro outstanding-loan figures, which could support an additive reading being intended throughout and make the IR's approach defensible by parallel construction. The ambiguity is genuine and not resolvable from the text alone, but a reviewer's numeric conclusion about available Maintenance Liquidity could differ materially depending on which reading is correct.

findings.verifierReasoning: The Maintenance Liquidity calculation depends on at least one input - the "Adjustment to Liquidity" figure - whose substantive value is defined entirely by an external, unretrieved Monthly Factoring Report, the same document whose unavailability caused the sibling definition "Invoice Restrictions" (compiled in the very same section) to be honestly marked MISSING_CONTEXT/UNSUPPORTED. In addition, no context items were retrieved for this candidate at all, and Phase 2 flagged a HIGH-severity issue that no anchoring structural node exists to retrieve context from, meaning none of the six dependent defined terms this definition relies on (including Cash Equivalents, Permitted Euro Revolving Indebtedness, Refinancing Indebtedness) were actually resolved or verified - every reference shows resolvedDefinitionId: null. Marking this definition COMPLETE while its sibling in the same passage was marked MISSING_CONTEXT for a comparable (indeed overlapping) external-document dependency is an internally inconsistent sufficiency judgment. This may be defensible if the intended standard is that the definition's own formula "shape" is fully stated in the amendment text (with only variable inputs left to external lookup, akin to referencing Consolidated EBITDA), but given the totality of unresolved dependencies and the Phase-2-flagged inability to retrieve any anchoring context, a COMPLETE label here deserves the heightened scrutiny called for by a confident-but-possibly-wrong sufficiency claim.
